status: Local changes only; not committed or pushed.
scope: Legacy and modern GM values, bulk operations, listeners, menu commands, URL include/exclude globs and document-body timing.

coverage: Legacy synchronous cache hydration and immediate writes; modern promise APIs and bulk defaults/deletion.
Cross-tab listener origin, persistence across new documents, listener/menu removal and disable revocation.
Native menu pointer and Tab/Enter input in all three browsers; Chrome/Edge actual worker-stop reconnection.
Native start/body/end/idle timing, include/match union, include-only query/fragment rules and noframes.
Ten simultaneous isolated cache/menu users; Chromium overflow fails before privileged source execution.
Unit tests cover storage failures, rollback, delayed acknowledgements, reentrant listeners, forged requests, quotas and shutdown pressure.
Existing native ad blocking and blocked-blank-tab cleanup regressions.
visualReview: Inspected Chrome and Firefox popup commands and Edge narrow manager; the final UI bytes match those reviewed. Earlier passes also reviewed desktop layouts.
resolvedFindings: Twelve simultaneous mocked cache starts reproduced the old per-tab admission failure; bounded startup admission is now separate from the unchanged value-request budgets. See bootstrap-before.out.

The matching menu-startup regression also reproduced queue saturation. Menu updates now have separate bounded admission, coalesce while one request is in flight per native connection, preserve ordinary value slots, and yield to manager controls. See menus-before.out.

Native Chromium allows ten isolated worlds per document. Broad include prefilters consumed unrelated worlds; native OR matching and conservative include globs now preserve scope. A reserved .invalid placeholder satisfies Chrome include-only registration schema without granting extra scope.

Firefox keyboard activation initially failed on a plain button too: the native permission prompt left browser focus outside content despite DOM activeElement. Explicitly focusing the owned selected browser fixed both Tab/Enter and menu tests.

Other retained harness failures include executable selection, bounded startup timeout, permission-checkbox handling, a diagnostic expression syntax error and a transient Chrome loadUnpacked timeout. No browser security protection was bypassed.
limits: Focused compatibility subset, not full Violentmonkey parity; no remote dependencies, resources, privileged network APIs or updates.
Synchronous legacy reads/listeners hydrate before source execution, which can delay document-start.
JSON-only storage and bounded queues; per-script native isolation remains subject to Chromium ten-world document limit.
Firefox shared compatibility/permission coverage does not duplicate the entire Chrome/Edge editor/import-export/worker-restart suite.
Offline results do not establish live-site compatibility or universal ad blocking; personal installed extension state was not changed.
